Yeah some devs need to learn difficulty does not just mean more hitpoints and stronger attacks.
This. I'd play Skyrim on master difficulty but really the game is no more interesting if I do, just more tedious.
That's because it's no different from the artificial level-scaled difficulty Oblivion suffered from, too.

I highly suggest this for playing the witcher 3. A Lot of the monster contracts are about building tension and it's way better if you have to find the right bombs, potions, and oils to barely survive a hard fight that you spent an hour tracking down. Really once you learn how the monsters move they aren't super hard to beat and it's rewarding being able to dance around their deadly attacks.
Definitely! Death March was the only way to play that game. I actually kind of wish it was tougher but maybe new game + will scratch that itch.

Actually I find that playing games on super hard difficulty makes a game into a technical challenge where often the spirit of the game, particularly the exploration, customization, and freedom of playstyle are lost as the game boils down to a much constrained particular set of choices that just happen to work on the highest difficulty. Often times it involves exploiting the AI or making use of tactics or skills that the devs hadn't considered or properly balanced when designing the game.

If I find a game too easy I will usually compensate by using poor tactics and having fun with it, setting my own goals, adding flavour to some of my characters while giving them technical handicaps. Much more rewarding.

I generally play on hard only when the game rewards me for the effort. I'm not (that much) into masochism, prefer taking things easy. People are different, there is no right or wrong way to play a game. Bragging rights or being a better player (whatever that means) do not really matter to me personally. More for my money? Maybe, but what if I'm not entertained by playing on sadomasochism difficulty? It's not fun if it becomes a chore.

It's really about what you want, apparently some people like grinding a boss 17 times in a row, others just want the story without too much challenge.

When enemies are just bullet sponges, normal is the way to go. Otherwise I would recommend playing on a harder difficulty. FEAR is a good example how to deal with difficulty. On harder difficulties the guns do more damage both ways. Enemies die faster but so do you. Bad way to do it is making enemies have way too much health or messing with the aim of the guns. Stalker made guns less accurate on easier difficulties, which actually made the game harder and more frustrating.
